answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a meadow as the anchor of the cost.
